description: This bar chart, from the paper "How Knowledge Popularity Influences and Enhances LLM Knowledge Boundary Perception," illustrates the "Popularity" of different knowledge categories for three large language models (LLaMA3, Qwen2, and ChatGPT), as well as two baseline conditions (Acc=0 & GT Ans and Acc=1 & GT Ans), across two domains: "Songs" and "Basketball". The vertical axis, labeled "Popularity," is scaled linearly from 60 to 220, with major gridlines and tick marks at intervals of 40. The horizontal axis presents the two domains, "Songs" on the left and "Basketball" on the right. Within each domain, there are six bars, each representing one of the five model/baseline conditions. The blue bars represent LLaMA3, the red bars represent Qwen2, and the yellow bars represent ChatGPT. The patterned bars represent the baseline conditions: the hatched bars represent "Acc=0 & GT Ans" and the cross-hatched bars represent "Acc=1 & GT Ans". All bars are grouped within their respective domain. The chart is not sorted; the bars are presented in the order of the legend. The bars for "Basketball" are significantly taller than those for "Songs," indicating higher popularity scores for basketball-related knowledge. For example, in the "Basketball" domain, the tallest bar is the red one for Qwen2, reaching approximately 220, while the shortest bar is the yellow one for ChatGPT, at approximately 160. In the "Songs" domain, the tallest bar is the blue one for LLaMA3, at approximately 120, while the shortest bar is the yellow one for ChatGPT, at approximately 80. There is no visual emphasis on any specific bar beyond the color and pattern coding defined by the legend.
